---
title: "Stage 3: Player Models for Shot Volume"
output: html_document
---

Results come from the pipeline (`targets::tar_make()` in the project root);
this report only reads and displays them. Models: M0 league, home, score and
player counts; M1 adds teams; M2 adds players without teams; M3 adds players as
deviations from team. Player effects are ridge-penalized.

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Run from the project root whether knit by tar_make() or by the Knit button
root <- normalizePath(if (file.exists("_targets.R")) "." else "..")
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r libraries}
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
tar_source()
```

```{r read}
cv3 <- tar_read(cv3)
effects3 <- tar_read(effects3)
```

## 1. Likelihood and sanity check

The team-only model is fit as Poisson on the stints; a Pearson dispersion of
`r DISPERSION_THRESHOLD` or more would switch to a negative binomial. Team
attack effects at the stint level should match the stage 1 model.

```{r family}
show_table(family_table(tar_read(fam3)))
show_table(tar_read(sanity3))
```

## 2. Do player effects predict better than teams alone?

Held-out deviance on 10 folds of whole matches (lower is better). The prior SD
is chosen on the same folds, so penalized gains are slightly optimistic.

```{r cv}
show_table(cv_table(cv3))
```

```{r cv-curve, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
plot_cv_curve(cv3)
```

## 3. Are player effects stable?

M3 fit separately on alternating matches; players with 300+ minutes in each half.

```{r reliability}
show_table(reliability_table(tar_read(split_half3)))
```

## 4. Player effects (M3)

Offense: higher means the team shoots more with the player on. Defense: lower
means the team concedes fewer shots. Interpret individual rankings only if
Section 3 shows meaningful reliability.

```{r effects}
show_table(effects_spread_table(effects3))
show_table(top_players_table(effects3, "Offense"))
show_table(top_players_table(effects3, "Defense"))
```
